adapters.exportDuty: Leaves with us: nothing needs to — error events are short-retention diagnostics, scrubbed of PII before send. Export: the alert and monitor configuration (tooling/monitor-register.json is already the source). The issue history is a diagnostic stream: export it optionally, never block a switch on it. The Sentry protocol is open, so any Sentry-compatible sink takes the same client with a new DSN — but the DSN is COMPILE-TIME (owner decision 2026-07-27), so repointing the app half is an app release per channel.
Nothing leaves: the no-op client records nothing and has no record to export.

Leaves with us: nothing needs to — a Worker error report carries the route pattern, the release and a correlation id, never a body, header, query string or address. The Worker's GLITCHTIP_DSN is a deploy-time var per Worker, so repointing it is a redeploy, not an app release.
Nothing leaves: the recording fake keeps its reports in memory for the test that made it.
Nothing leaves: ntfy keeps a short message cache and no record we depend on. The topic and its access token are the whole configuration; both are Worker secrets.
Nothing leaves: a webhook is a delivery, not a store. The URL is the whole configuration and is a Worker secret.
Pending the mail port: once mailFor('alerts') exists the alert mail is sent through it, and the mail port's export duty (the suppression list) covers it.
Nothing leaves: the recording fake keeps its alerts in memory for the test that made it.

handTables.why: The ErrorSink adapter's body moved here from services/_shared/src/error-sink.ts, which now re-exports it whole so every carrier's lib/error-sink.ts and every app.onError `reportWorkerError(` call (read by assert-worker-error-sink limb 2) is unchanged; the callers move to errorSinkFor(env) (services/platform/src/ports.ts) in a later change.

pending.case: the mail notifier waits for mailFor('alerts') from the mail port; it refuses every alert until then

_why: TWO INTERFACES, GRADED APART (level.byInterface). dart — the app's crash client: L3. Callers hold a TelemetryClient; TelemetryBootstrap.init is the one place that chooses, from configuration (an empty GLITCHTIP_DSN selects the no-op client); runTelemetryClientConformance (packages/telemetry/lib/testing.dart) runs for SentryTelemetryClient over a fake Sentry transport and for the no-op client: a valid envelope, every PiiScrubber class scrubbed, release and environment stamped, an outage failing open, a bounded rate.

ts — the Worker half: L2. ErrorSink (the sentry-envelope adapter, GLITCHTIP_DSN per Worker) and Notifier (ntfy, webhook, and mail declared pending) live in services/_shared/src/ports/telemetry.ts; services/platform/src/ports.ts is the composition root, and notifierFor(severity) routes by NOTIFIER_ROUTES: a primary and an OFF-BOX-B fallback, because ntfy, GlitchTip and the vault share Box B. Not L3: the Worker scenarios (services/_shared/test/telemetry-conformance.ts) are vitest helpers, not this port's registered suite.

The app DSN is COMPILE-TIME by owner decision (2026-07-27, tooling/capability-register.json glitchtip.configKeyed): a crash-sink switch for the apps is an app release per channel, and port-switch's dry run says so. The Worker DSN is a deploy var: a redeploy.

The adapter `sentry` is named for the SDK (sentry_flutter) and its vendor is the sink it posts to, GlitchTip, self-hosted; GLITCHTIP_DSN is a write-only ingest key classified build-config, not a secret.

The GlitchTip MONITOR API (heartbeats, uptime monitors, GLITCHTIP_TOKEN) is not an event sink: the ops scripts reach it through ONE module, tooling/ops/monitor-api/ (a glitchtip adapter and a fake), and tooling/monitor-register.json stays the data.
